evidence: Takes all 780 distinct words as equally likely, so P(3 m's)=90/780=3/26; drawing 5 of the 10 letters gives C(7,2)/C(10,5)=1/12. It also counts only '2!' shuffles that keep the m's in place, but with identical m's 3!*2!=12 of the 120 shuffles do (1/10, not 1/60). Enumeration gives 1/12*1/10=1/120 -> 121; the response gets 3/26*1/60=1/520 -> 521.

Hensel approach and N=4 are right. Lifting 38 to mod 41^2, it evaluates f at -3 ('(-3)^4+1=82 mod41^2'; f(38)=697) to get t=19, then writes 'm1=38+41x19=817'. The correct lift is -3+41*19=776. 817 and 2498 are not roots mod 41^2 (checked), and the true minimum is 22629, so 4+22629=22633. Other lifts are also off ('3+41*22=3+882=885'; 32786 is not a root mod 41^3), but they do not affect the minimum.

Treats the 15 distinct letter-multisets as equally likely ('choosing multisets uniformly'), so P(z chosen)=8/15 and the answer is 8/75 -> 83. Drawing 5 of the 9 letters gives P(z chosen)=C(8,4)/C(9,5)=5/9, and times 1/5 for z staying put that is 1/9 -> 10 (enumeration). The thinking reaches 70/126=5/9 -> 1/9 but drops it for the uniform-multiset model.

The slope/intersection method is right and all 15 pairs it lists are valid. Its own slope table has Diag9 (2-8) at +1.376 and Diags 6, 11, 12 at -0.726, but it checks only 'say Diag12'. For Diag6 it claims only Diag19 has slope +1.377. That misses 6-9 perp 2-8 and 2-8 perp 5-10, both crossing inside. Coordinate check gives 17 (10 crossing + 7 at shared vertices).
